title: Characterisation of lung function trajectories and associated early-life predictors in an Australian birth cohort study.
ehr_evidence: Our study included participants from the Raine Study, a prospective pregnancy cohort, with at least two spirometry measurements.
summary: Longitudinal birth cohort study characterizing lung function trajectories (FEV1, FVC, FEV1/FVC) from age 6 to 22 and identifying early-life predictors including asthma, maternal smoking, and air pollution exposure.
key_findings: Childhood asthma at age 6 was associated with a low FEV1 trajectory (RRR 1.68, 95% CI 1.20–2.36).
Pre- and postnatal maternal smoking was associated with a very low FEV1/FVC trajectory (RRR 2.47, 95% CI 1.52–3.90).
Early-life PM2.5Absorbance exposure was associated with a low FEV1 trajectory (RRR 1.63, 95% CI 1.06–2.51).
Early-life PM2.5Absorbance exposure was associated with an average–low FEV1/FVC trajectory (RRR 0.52, 95% CI 0.35–0.79).
Early-life NO2 exposure was associated with an average–low FEV1/FVC trajectory (RRR 0.90, 95% CI 0.84–0.96).
Low birthweight was associated with a low–average FEV1/FVC trajectory (RRR 2.03, 95% CI 1.11–3.71).
Childhood aeroallergens or combined food allergies were associated with an average–low FEV1/FVC trajectory (RRR 0.70, 95% CI 0.51–0.95).
study_design: Prospective birth cohort study with group-based trajectory modeling
population: 1512 participants from the Raine Study, followed from age 6 to 22 years in Western Australia
exposure_domain: Early-life environmental exposures (air pollution, maternal smoking), clinical factors (asthma, atopy, infections), and sociodemographic/birth characteristics
limitations: High dropout rate with symptom-biased retention
Reliance on parental recall for respiratory infections
Back-extrapolation of air pollution models over 19 years without antenatal data
Exclusion of pregnancy complications due to small numbers
data_availability_statement: Please note: supplementary material is not edited by the Editorial Office, and is uploaded as it has been supplied by the author.
